Why go for something we don't know how long it could take with especially huge datasets possible instead of something we know how long it will take( O(n) )?

How about: 

`var objectFromPairs = arr => arr.reduce((a,b) => (a[b[0]] = b[1], a), {})`

or 

`var objectFromPairs = arr => arr.reduce((a,b) => { a[b[0]] = b[1]; return a;}, {})`

The first variant is quite easy to read. Is it any faster performance-wise than the original one? (just curious) I would definitely prefer the `.reduce()` variant, though in terms of readability as even the original one I had implemented felt wrong to me somehow.

Although the ES6 version is an interesting implementation, I feel that the `.reduce()` version is more readable. I would assume that the `.reduce()` version would perform marginally better since it doesn't create intermediary arrays and objects.
Right, so we'll stick with `reduce()`.
